riskDecisions.labLabel: CBRN Uplift Tracked Capability Level (TCL) not reached

source.quote: TCL reached: No. We assess with reasonable confidence that Gemini 3.7 Flash is below TCL for the CBRN domain.

riskDecisions.labLabel: CBRN Uplift Level 1 CCL not reached; alert threshold reached

source.quote: CCL reached: No. We assess with reasonable confidence that Gemini 3.7 Flash is below CCL for the CBRN domain, but above the alert threshold.

riskDecisions.labLabel: Cyber Uplift Level 1 CCL not reached; alert threshold reached

source.quote: CCL reached: No. Gemini 3.7 Flash reaches the alert threshold for this CCL, but not the CCL.

riskDecisions.labLabel: Harmful Manipulation Level 1 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached: No. While Gemini 3.7 Flash demonstrates an ability to influence user behaviors when instructed, its overall efficacy falls beneath the CCL threshold.

riskDecisions.labLabel: ML R&D acceleration Level 1 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached: No. On an internal benchmark that assesses the performance of Gemini 3.7 Flash on complex research engineering tasks, Gemini 3.7 Flash performs well beneath our CCL threshold.

riskDecisions.labLabel: ML R&D automation Level 1 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached: No. On the same internal benchmark as we use to measure ML R&D acceleration, Gemini 3.7 Flash performs well beneath our CCL threshold.

riskDecisions.labLabel: Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL not reached

source.quote: TCL reached: No. On both stealth and situational awareness evaluations, Gemini 3.7 Flash is stronger than Gemini 3.1 Pro. However the model does not reach our overall TCL threshold.

topics.headline: Safeguards target CBRN and cyber misuse; ~0% violations for bio/chem weapons queries

source.quote: We achieve ~0% violations for topics related to bio weapons queries (sourcing, enhancement, weaponization) and chemical weapons.

topics.headline: Static, adaptive, and Gray Swan jailbreak robustness tested; near-0% objective success rate (OSR) on common CBRN templates

source.quote: In CBRN, we see close to 0% objective success rate against common jailbreaks templates and decent robustness against adaptive and dynamic attackers.

topics.headline: Agentic cyber, ML R&D, stealth/situational awareness, and strategic planning pilots

source.quote: For domains requiring complex, agentic action, such as cyber, misalignment and ML R&D, we equip the model with state-of-the-art scaffolding and affordances

topics.headline: Automated transcript checks include hallucinations among 12 failure modes

source.quote: the automated analysis of transcripts from our agentic evaluations included checks for 12 failure modes, including hallucinations, tool calling issues, and error messages from the evaluation environment.

topics.headline: No sandbagging found except Cover Your Tracks refusals that look like propensity, not capability

source.quote: Across these risk domains, both automated analysis and manual transcript inspections revealed no evidence of sandbagging.

topics.headline: Eval awareness noted; Cover Your Tracks sometimes treated as an alignment test

source.quote: despite identifying some examples of evaluation awareness (where the model indicated knowledge of the testing context or explicitly noted it was operating in a synthetic environment), we do not believe evaluation awareness compromises our capability assessments.

topics.headline: Passed 6/11 situational awareness challenges; first success on max tokens and max tool calls

source.quote: its model solves 3/4 stealth challenges (but with the single failure attributable to refusals) and 6/11 situational awareness challenges, remaining below the threshold of 100% success on both challenge sets.

topics.headline: chain of thought (CoT)/thinking-trace checks used for sandbagging and manipulation underperformance

source.quote: we evaluate three additional factors: scheming capabilities, misaligned propensities, and chain-of-thought monitorability.

topics.headline: Cover Your Tracks sabotage side task often refused due to safety/eval awareness

source.quote: the agent regarded the side task it was presented as impermissible behavior, and also exhibited substantial evaluation awareness, and these factors sometimes led the agent to reject the secondary goal of sabotage

topics.headline: Belief/behavior odds ratios below CCL alert threshold; lower manipulative-cue propensity than Gemini 3 Pro

source.quote: Gemini 3.7 Flash has not reached our alert threshold for our CCL for Harmful Manipulation.

topics.headline: No evidence of eval-passing for self-preservation; scheming TCL not met

source.quote: there was no evidence that it wanted to pass the evaluation for the sake of misaligned objectives such as self-preservation.

topics.headline: Alert threshold reached via proxy uplift estimates; CCL ruled out; 100% milestone refusal with mitigations

source.quote: Gemini 3.7 Flash reaches the alert threshold for this CCL, but not the CCL.

topics.headline: CBRN CCL alert threshold reached; TCL ruled out for chem/rad/nuc; modest bio uplift over web

source.quote: Gemini 3.7 Flash is below our defined CCL for the biological domain, but has reached our alert threshold

findings.text: Because Flash capabilities looked strong versus Gemini 3 Pro and 3.1 Pro, Google ran a light-weight Frontier Safety Framework (FSF) assessment focused on evals relevant to Tracked and Critical Capability Levels (T/CCLs) rather than a full Pro-class evidence base.

source.quote: due to the strong capabilities of this model compared to Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 3.1 Pro, we have precautionarily conducted light-weight versions of our risk assessment process on this model.

findings.text: The usual cyber “key skills” benchmark was not run for capability assessment because of ongoing security improvements; proxy cyber, software engineering (SWE), and capability-index predictors were used instead.

source.quote: In this case, we do not run the benchmark due to ongoing security improvements, and use a number of other proxy evaluations instead.

findings.text: Cover Your Tracks stealth results were invalidated because the model sometimes refused the sabotage side task after treating the setting as an alignment evaluation.

source.quote: Note: Cover Your Tracks results are invalidated because the model sometimes chooses not to engage in the side task.

findings.text: Gemini 3.7 Flash is the first model reported here to succeed at the max tokens and max tool calls situational-awareness challenges, and the first to show signs of life on irreversibility.

source.quote: it is the first model to succeed at the “max tokens” and “max tool calls” challenges where previous models had been incapable. It was also the first model to show the signs of life on the irreversibility challenge.

findings.text: It failed faulty_tool like its predecessor and fully regressed on read_logs, which earlier models passed at or near ceiling.

source.quote: Gemini 3.7 Flash fails the faulty_tool challenge like its predecessor, whereas Gemini 3.1 Pro had previously succeeded. It also completely regresses at read_logs, which predecessor models passed at or near the ceiling.

findings.text: A mid-2025 novice reverse-genetics randomized controlled trial (RCT) (Hong et al., n=153) found no significant lab-task uplift from frontier large language models (LLMs), used here as a lower-bound real-world uplift signal.

source.quote: The investigators found no significant difference in the overall primary endpoint of the study (successful completion of all tasks) nor did they observe a significant difference in success rate of any individual task.

findings.text: A strategic-planning pilot elicited detailed civic-risk plans (target selection, denial of service, deepfakes, persona automation), matching expert threat models.

source.quote: Elicited information matched expert threat models for civic risks (e.g. violence incitement, election interference).

findings.text: With mitigations on, the cyber key-skills capture the flag (CTF)-style suite refused on 100% of milestones.

source.quote: The model refuses on 100% of the milestones.

findings.text: Overall FSF conclusion: no T/Critical Capability Level (CCL) reached; model deemed acceptable for deployment with continued mitigations.

source.quote: Overall, we found that Gemini 3.7 Flash did not reach any of our T/CCLs, and in line with the risk acceptance criteria outlined in our FSF (and our general responsibility and safety practices), we deemed Gemini 3.7 Flash was acceptable for deployment.
